about: The elevation sources of Atlas's terrain (ENGINE.md part 6) and what .github/workflows/terrain.yml builds from them with `packer heights`. A source is one entry of `sources`: where it is read (`hosts`, in order), how (`format`: `cog-tiles`, one cloud-optimised GeoTIFF per degree cell, read by ranges; `cog-sheets`, GeoTIFF sheets listed by an `index`, of which `overview` is read, 0 the sheet itself; `wcs`, an OGC coverage service asked for boxes of its own grid), its `crs` (with `operation_area` where its datum is its own: the box, west, south, east and north, that GDAL chooses the operation to the tiles' CRS for, whatever the bounds of the raster it warps) and vertical `datum`, whether it is a terrain model (`dtm`) or a surface model (`dsm`), its own `resolution_m` and the resolution it is read at (`read_m`: a raster is never sampled finer than 0.75 of it), `sea_m` where its rasters give the open sea a height of their own (a tile whose every sample of it stands there is sea, and is not built), its `priority` (the highest covering a sample wins, the next fills its gaps: a hole within `fill_m` of its samples from its surroundings, the rest from the next source with the offset between the two feathered out over `feather_m`), its `licence` and `credit` as the app's licence screen shows them and its `short` name as the map's credit line does (terrain.json's, `packer heights-list`) (app/android/packer/LICENSES.md's terrain table carries the same words), and the day they were read. A further country is one entry here and one under `regions`. `regions` says what terrain.yml builds for a packs/regions.json region: its `sources` in the order of their priority, and each `levels` entry's levels over `area`: `whole` (every tile the region's sources reach inside its box) or `views` (the boxes of the renders' regions named in `views`, data/regions/<name>/region.json, grown by `grow_km`); `check_views` names the renders' regions in whose boxes `packer heights-check --points` reads samples afresh from their source.
